record.original_question: . Given a graded vector spaceV= L∞ i=0 Vi and a graded linear operatorDon it where D(V0) ={0}andD(V i+1)⊂D(V i−1), is it always possible to define a bilinear product onVthat turns it into a graded algebra with identity for whichDis a derivation —D(ab) =D(a)b+aD(b)? It seems that one can always define such a product, but there is much freedom and no clear guarantee the product has any nice properties. So let us add that the product must be associative. If this product exists, it allows the graded linear operatorDto be used to construct a dual graded graph by the construction in the citation.

artifact.status_search_result: A web search located Fomin's foundational works on dual graded graphs ("Duality of Graded Graphs", 1994; "Schensted Algorithms for Dual Graded Graphs", 1995) and follow-ups on duality through operads, but no source was found that resolves the precise question of when a degree-$-1$ operator on a non-negatively graded vector space admits an associative graded unital product making it a derivation. The status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Duality of Graded Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Fomin's 1994 paper introducing dual graded graphs via linear operators on graded vector spaces satisfying a commutation relation.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the original framework in which the derivation question arises, but does not address existence of an associative algebra structure for arbitrary (V,D).

status_evidence.title: Duality of Graded Graphs Through Operads
status_evidence.snippet: Develops algebraic constructions of dual graded graphs from operads, providing classes of examples but not a general existence theorem for the derivation question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats specific algebraic constructions, leaving the general existence question unaddressed.
